correctness.rationale: Every selected doubled subdivision incidence identifies one matching edge of the original graph, and different double-incidence vertices have disjoint original endpoints. After deleting these matched endpoints, selected single incidences have original centers C and opposite original endpoints in U, with no other restrictions. This is an invertible partition of all packings and proves the complete edge-size generating function for every finite simple G (empty/disconnected allowed). Maximizing selected incidences gives 2|M|+maxcut(G−V(M)); for K_n the endpoint maximum of f_n(k)=2k+floor((n−2k)^2/4) yields floor(n²/4) at n>=5 and balanced ordered cut extremizers, with separately evaluated n<=4 exceptions. A fresh conflict-graph subset enumerator checked each of 75 labelled simple graphs through 4 vertices and K5 coefficients (1,20,130,340,355,120,20), agreeing with the independently implemented matching/center formula. Enumeration supports, but is not a replacement for, the general bijection.
residual_risks: Only one-subdivisions of finite simple graphs; the general evaluation may be exponential; no claim about multiple edges or arbitrary subdivision depth.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The cited graph-packing and injective-edge-colouring literature treats maximum size on other host families or partition of all host edges, not a single EOP class on an arbitrary full subdivision; no established stronger theorem found that determines all coefficients in (1) or the K_n oriented optimum census.
